A brief history of Dash and Jay:

When Jay-Z was a young street hustler coming up, it took DJ Clark Kent to recognise his ability stretched beyond the streets and in to the rap world.

Clark Kent introduced Jay and Dame, and set off a relationship that will be forever etched in hip hop history.

Dame was described as the ideas man. He was the brash, cocky businessman who would facilitate and enterprise his way in to business meetinings with labels, attempting to nail down a distribution deal for Rocafella Records.

Dash’s ideas propelled Rocafella to new levels, through things like ROC Films, Rocawear and ArmadalE Vodka.

There were wide reports of tension though, mainly after the Backstage tour film came out, during the Hard Knock Life tour of 1999. Dame was seen to be taking over, and when Dame promoted Cam'Ron to Vice President whilst Jay was away holidaying the relationship basically ended.

Interesting, in his Breakfast Club interview Kanye mentioned that a lot of great records came out of that tension that was inherent in Rocafella at the time.

meaning:
Zack O'Malley’s book Empire State of Mind was incredibly instructive in explaining the way this particular deal worked for Jay and for The Nets.

Jay paid a reported $4.5m for his stake in The New Jersey Nets. The plan was always to bring The Nets to Brooklyn, with the opening of the huge Barclays Centre just a stones throw from where Jay grew up in Marcy.

His history with the franchise is looked upon cynically by many, with some claiming that his ownership was merely symbolic. His campaign to sign LeBron James fell by the wayside, and Angela is referring to the period from when The Nets knew they were moving from New Jersey to Brooklyn, during which they were getting only around 1000 people turning up to home games. Jay was one who stayed away during that torrid period of time.

Say what you will about it, Jay’s name helped save The Barclays Centre. When Bruce Ratner, the developer, ran in to hard times, it was Jay’s name that attracted Russian Mikhail Prokhorov to the table with a huge investment that put the centre back on track for its 2012 opening.

At the time of the interview, this may still have been the case, as most reports of Jay’s stake being sold came out in September, a few months after this interview took place.

Jay was set to rake in about $1.5m from the sale.

Rolling Stone even reported that he also sold his stake in the centre because it was tied up with his Nets deal.

As of 2015, Jay Z does not have a business stake in either The Nets or The Barclays Centre.

vault_lines: Jay: I liked it
meaning:
Part of Jay’s New Rules campaign involved a new way of distributing his record, and one that essentially ensured it would go platinum on its release date.

The deal was made with Samsung, for somewhere in the region of $20 million, in which the company would essentially ‘buy’ 1 million copies of the record, and give them away for free for customers who downloaded an app prior to the release date. These users would recieve the album 3 days prior to its physical release date.

Unfortunately, the initiative was plagued with problems, even prompting the twitter hashtag #SaumsungFail to trend. The app crashed and there were several other problems, but as Jay said, he had to take the hit so that others can now move forward with this form of release. It has the immediate advantage of securing a concrete sales figure before the record even goes on sale, which you could argue is the only way Jay could’ve posted such huge numbers in todays climate.

meaning:
Jay has had several high profile beefs, some of which have arguably ended (or at least diminished) careers.

His beef with Cam'Ron, goes way back to 1997. A full description can be found here, but certainly since he left RocaFella and began releasing albums under his own Diplomats label, his sales have been significantly weaker. Meaning he used to sell platinum, now he barely sells 100k copies.

Beanie Siegel is a very interesting one. Again, a full description can be found here, but essentially Beans did it to himself. He took the side of Damon Dash when the RocaFella split occurred, and his issues with Kanye did little to help his commercial career. Again, as he did with Cam'Ron, Jay shouts this beef out in the verse he did on “Poundcake”.

Jay’s list of dead careers also extends to his business and hustle dealings, with guys like Jaz-O, DeHaven, Kareem Burke and Dame Dash all being left behind, somewhat worse off than when they began their lives with Jay. He has, indeed, put a few careers on hold.

song: Jay Z on The Breakfast Club (Power 105.1)
line: The great thing about it is that it didn’t destroy either of your careers CTG: It helped Nas! AY: Yeah it did help him at that time. But for both of you it’s not like ‘ok, now this guy just destroyed me’ cause that happens sometimes with beef, but you guys both were still successful after that, you even more so
vault_lines: AY: The great thing about it is that it didn't destroy either of your careers
meaning:
Both “Ether” and “Takeover” appeared on records that are now considered classics, Stillmatic and The Blueprint, and the beef was certainly helpful in building buzz around the records and propelling their sales.

Whether it helped Nas more than Jay is a subjective topic. It didn’t hinder either of them, and arguably both of them were still being spoken of as the greatest rappers alive before those two records came out. Since then, of course, Jay Z went on to record his third classic, The Black ALbum, and has gone from strength to strength as a business man.

Nas has released a slew of records that have hovered between hot and lukewarm, however he is still regarded as one of the top lyricists in the game. The only thing to be sure is that, unlike a lot of other beef’s, most blatantly the 50 Cent and Murder Inc. beef, no-ones career was ended or curtailed.

Whilst this is not the most revealing thing Jay says in this interview, it is very interesting to get an insiders point of view on the critical process of reviewing music. Certainly, during the late 90s and early 2000s, when publications like XXL and The Source were at their zenith, reviews played a much bigger role. The internet was not yet at the cutting edge of record releases, and physical copies were still being consumed in rampant fashion.

Nowadays, there are a plethora of review sites, and an infinite amount of blogs that exist in personal spaces to review almost every record that is released. It does lose the magic somewhat, and Beyonce and Drake have proven that long lead-in times are completely irrelevant when you drop surprise records.

meaning:
During Kanye’s 2013 Breakfast Club interview Charlamagne and Kanye got in to it over Kanye’s representation of corporations and brands in music. Kanye’s main agenda seemed to be to denounce these huge corporate organisms, and to claim that they were in fact stealing the soul and freedom of black people from them by charging them exorbitant prices to wear certain clothing, and by using artists as branding machines.

Despite Kanye’s increasing presence in the fashion industry, his belief is that by infiltrating these corporations on every level, he will be able to provide for his fellow rappers on a basic financial level.

Jay Z is cut from a different cloth. In Zack O'Malley’s excellent book Empire State of Mind he rarely goes in to Jay’s philanthropic side, happily focusing on his ruthless business acumen, which is much more about accumulating personal wealth than taking down corporations from the inside. Jay’s lyrics are laced with corporate imagery, and websites have dedicated themselves to tracking his various and copious brand shout outs.

In another Biggie moment, Jay recalls the MC making a cameo appearance in the video for "Ain’t No N—-a,” which Jay was filming with Foxy Brown in Miami in 1996. line: Cops want to knock me, D.A. wanna box me in But somehow, I beat them charges like Rocky
vault_lines: Cops want to knock me, D.A. wanna box me in
meaning:
Jay is leaning into his criminal past here, saying that while he’s been attacked by the law and put on trial, no criminal charges have ever stuck to him and resulted in his punishment.

“Beating charges like Rocky” refers more specifically to a boxing simile. It is likely referencing Rocky Balboa, the titular character of the “Rocky” films starring Sylvester Stalone.



In the film, Rocky both boxes, and is famous for training by punching sides of beef, perhaps lending to Jay the idea of “beating” something.



However, that line could also be referencing real-life boxer Rocky Marciano, the heavyweight who never lost a fight. The idea of a perfect streak seems like it would appeal to JAY-Z, so this is certainly a viable reference.

line: H to the izz-O, V to the izz-A
vault_lines: That's the anthem, get'cha damn hands up
meaning:
Sean Carter is known by many names. One of them mentioned here, HOVA, is a religious allusion to God, known in Hebrew as “Jehova”.

JAY+HOVA = JAY-HOVA or Jehova.

This apparently stems from an MTV interview where Carter described Jay-Hova as a title bestowed upon him by those impressed with his ability to lay down songs quickly, and without any written lyrics. However, to avoid people thinking that he was calling himself a god, he shortened the nickname to “Young Hova”.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aKcW6Jrhm2M&feature=emb_logo

line: Not guilty, y’all got to feel me
vault_lines: That's the anthem, get'cha damn hands up
meaning:
Jay-Z was accused of stabbing record executive Lance “Un” Rivera for what Jay-Z perceived was Rivera’s bootlegging of Vol. 3… Life and Times of S. Carter. The stabbing allegedly occurred at the record release party for Q-Tip’s debut solo album Amplified at the Kit Kat Klub, a now-defunct night club in Times Square

Jay-Z initially denied the incident and pleaded not guilty when a grand jury returned the indictment. Jay-Z and his lawyers contended he was nowhere around Rivera during the incident and they had witnesses and videotape evidence from the club that showed Jay-Z’s whereabouts during the disturbance. Nevertheless, he later pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor charge that resulted in a sentence of three years probation

vault_lines: Succeed in this rap game: the two things that's great
meaning:
In subsequent years Jay has pulled back on his thoughts on failure.

But I will not lose, for even in defeat
There’s a valuable lesson learned, so it evens up for me

His business career post-2001 is littered with false starts, so failure is something he learned to embrace.

His success up to 2001 was immense, it would only intensify dramatically after the release of this track.

line: I’ve seen Hoop Dreams deflate like a true fiend’s weight
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
Jay has seen kids in the ghetto with aspirations to be a basketball star ruined, either by violence or prison.

A true fiend (someone addicted to crack) loses a lot of weight. The word “deflate” also evokes a mental image of a basketall losing air.

Weight is also slang for money, “getting ya weight up.” A true drug fiend’s money is going to deflate because all of his money is going towards drugs.

Another interpretation is “weight” as slang for drugs, which a true fiend would go through very quickly.

Also, Hoop Dreams is a 1994 documentary following two basketball prospects in Chicago and their dream of becoming professional basketball players.

line: So you know I seen it all before
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
In 2014 Jay dropped a guest verse on Jeezy’s track “Seen It All”, expressing this very sentiment.

Park 92 bricks in front of 560 State
Now the Nets a stone throw from where I used to throw bricks
So it’s only right I’m still tossing ‘round Knicks

Jeezy later did an interview explaining how real these stories are for Jay.

We got on the phone and [Jay] was like, ’Yo, Jeezy, when I was writing the verse I had tears in my eyes, man,’ because it took him so far back to Marcy, every bar in that song was real — I put my hand on the bible.

line: Me under a lamppost, why I got my hand closed? That’s in my palm, watching the long arm of the law
vault_lines: That's in my palm, watching the long arm of the law
meaning:
Note the play on words with hand, palm and arm. Jay wouldn’t choose to say “watching the long arm of the law” for no reason.

Fans have also pointed out a potential double entendre here:
1. I have “cracks in my palm” (Jay Z has dry hands)
2. “Crack’s in my palm” (I’m dealing drugs.)

During the live version Jay replaces “crack” with “that” to adhere to MTV’s anti-cursing crusade.

line: Lookouts on the corner focused on the ave Ladies in the window, focused on the kinfolk
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
In the 80s a trend emerged where kids performed as lookouts for drug dealers. They’d stand on the corner of a block, with a view of all the roads leading to the strip a dealer was trading, and watch for police.

“Kinfolk” means family. Mothers, girlfriends, wives and sisters would observe the daily moves of their family, praying they wouldn’t be arrested, or worse.

This was a precursor to the lyrics on “What We Talkin' Bout,” in which Jay actually denounces hustling. Here he is observational, but this eventually turns to disgust.

Ain’t nothing cool about carrying a strap
Bout worrying your moms and burying your best cat

line: I was raised in the projects, roaches and rats Smokers out back selling their mama’s sofa
vault_lines: Smokers out back selling their mama's sofa
meaning:
Specifically Apartment 4B. Right in the heart of Marcy Projects.

Utilising two double meanings to highlight the poverty he faced. Roaches can mean both marijuana cigarettes and cockroaches, and rats refer to both the vermin and those who snitch on dealers, making the location even more fraught.

A crack addict will do anything for a fix. It’s depressing to think of someone selling their mothers possessions for drugs, but it was reality for those in the Projects.

line: Hov is back, life stories told through rap They acting like I sold you crack Like I told you sell drugs; no, Hov did that So hopefully you won’t have to go through that
vault_lines: Hov is back, life stories told through rap
meaning:
He raps about his experiences selling crack so you can get the experience without going out there and doing it themselves. But just because he is talking about crime, he isn’t endorsing it.
He is addressing accusations of poorly representing his community and perpetuating a glorification of criminal behaviour. There’s a scene in Fade To Black where he addresses this explicitly, saying he provides both sides of the argument: pleasure and pain.

During “Dope Man” Jay directly addresses the claim that he promotes criminal behaviour.

How come, you label your brand of dope
“Volume 1” and spread it through the slums?
Fed it to the young with total disregard
Your honor, the State seeks the maximum charge

line: We can talk, but money talks, so talk more bucks
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
The power of Roc-A-Fella records at the time was obvious. He was hailed as “The King of Rap” by news outlets, and his influence was huge.

Dame was quoted at the time:

Entrepreneurial, hustler, say it whatever you want to say it – just that hunger to make money, and to make your situation better.

Jay is willing to sit down and have a conversation with those he feels have wronged him, but as long as there are dollar signs involved, otherwise there’s no point.

line: Pay us like you owe us for all the years that you hoed us
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
Jay is accusing record executives of treating rappers like hoes. Eerily similar to Kendrick Lamar’s message on To Pimp A Butterfly.

Hoed is also a near homophone of hold. Many record labels hold artists back, deciding not to release records that an artist has slaved hard over in case of poor sales. This was an issue for The LOX and their relationship with Bad Boy Entertainment.

It could also refer to slavery, and the way Black people were held against their will, forced to work for zero pay. His opening line is “I do this for my culture.”

line: Label owners hate me, I’m raising the status quo up I’m overcharging labels for what they did to the Cold Crush
vault_lines: Label owners hate me, I'm raising the status quo up
meaning:
“Status quo” means the existing state of affairs. At the time label owners were hurting artists with harsh contracts and withholding payments of royalties.

As the owner of a major rap label, Jay now has industry clout. When other labels come to him for features or distribution deals, he keeps his own prices extra high as payback. “Rappers Delight”, one of the earliest rap songs, originally by Grandmaster Caz, a member of The Cold Crush Brothers, was just one example of artists not receiving their due compensation for work they did.

line: Show them how to move in a room full of vultures Industry is shady, it needs to be taken over
vault_lines: Show them how to move in a room full of vultures
meaning:
Throughout his career, Jay has criticised the establishment of the music industry. In ‘96, he called for black-owned record labels; in 2015, he launched a high-royalty streaming service to compete with Spotify. That’s consistent with metaphorically comparing the music industry head to vultures – disgusting scavengers, eating the flesh of struggling artists. Jay is trying to show other artists how to handle the corporate world – by dominating it.

Note the similarity to a Q-Tip line from “Check The Rhime” by A Tribe Called Quest:

Industry rule number four thousand and eighty
Record company people are shady

Although this line is often interpreted as a shot at Eminem, also known as Slim Shady, this is unlikely. Eminem featured on “Renegade”, so it’s unlikely Jay had beef with him. “Shady” is just a part of his lexicon.

line: I do this for my culture To let them know what ya boy look like when ya boy in that Roadster
vault_lines: I do this for my culture
meaning:
Even in 2001 he recognised his life story and his achievements were something to aspire to for young Black males. Not only that, the mention of “culture” adds a hip hop edge, and his business dealings and eventual success map out the “blueprint” for young rappers to follow in their career.

A “roaster” implies pressure. Jay isn’t talking down or claiming his race hasn’t faced struggle, he’s explaining just how resourceful, strong, and independent his race can be when under pressure.

Roaster is also a near homophone of “roadster”, and Jay expressed a penchant for expensive cars during this period.



For the live version Jay explicitly says “roadster”, and swaps “n-” for “ya boy” to adhere to MTV’s rules against cuss words.

The message plays off “Cogito ergo sum”, a proposition by Descartes that states “I think, therefore I am.” Anyone not feeling Jay doesn’t exist in his mind, and so ceases to exist.

‘'Vamoose’‘ comes from spanish ’‘vamos’‘, which means ’‘let’s go’‘ “Vamoose” is also the name of a bus line that runs direct service between NYC and the Maryland/DC/Virginia area, (which started running 3 years after this song was recorded)

In the live version of this track Jay allows his audience to spit the final line in an attempt to avoid cussing.

line: Still not guilty,
vault_lines: Still not guilty y'all got to feel me
meaning:
“Not guilty” has been a refrain on multiple Jay songs, from “22 Two’s” to “Guilty Until Proven Innocent.” It’s unclear what legal troubles he faced during 1996 when “22 Two’s” was recorded. The case “Guilty Until Proven Innocent” refers to is much easier to trace, his legal stoush with Lance Rivera would be at the forefront of his mind.

Jay pleaded guilty to those charges just months before the release of The Blueprint, receiving 3 years probation.

line: Cops want to knock me, D.A. wants to box me in But somehow I beat them charges like Rocky
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
Police want to “knock” (arrest) Jay and the District Attorney wants to put him in jail.

Rocky Balboa, the fictional boxing hero of the Rocky movies, dodged his share of punches from his fighting opponents.



Tried to “box me in”, I “beat” them charges like Rocky. He describes his fight with the law as a boxing metaphor. One of Jay’s favourite sports is boxing, he spoke about it extensively in Decoded and expanded into boxing management with his Roc Nation Sports arm.

His trial for the alleged stabbing of Lance “Un” Rivera wasn’t him beating the charges, rather he took probation by pleading guilty, in the knowledge if he had attempted a not guilty plea he may have faced jail time.

line: Haters want me clap that chrome, it ain’t easy
vault_lines: Haters want me clap that chrome, it ain't easy
meaning:
For the live version Jay flips his lyrics slightly. Instead of being clapped, his haters want him to do the clapping, resulting in a felony charge and removing him from the game, allowing other’s to take his place on the throne.

Prior to the recording of this show Jay actually did catch some legal heat, slapped with 3 years probation for stabbing Lance Rivera in 1999.

line: Wasn’t born hustlers, I was birthing ’em
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
A play on the “born hustler” idea in rap: drug-dealing can’t be taught, you have to grow up in the ghetto to do it well. You learn from experience, not books or schools.

Jay-Z was a supplier, he was turning his middlemen into hustlers.

In Decoded Jay explained the nature of passing his skills on to the younger generation:

They know that if they find the right kid, they can put him under their tutelage and he’ll get it fast, step right into the rhythm of the life. If that sounds predatory, it’s because recruiting new workers is one of the most predatory aspects of the game. When you’re doing it, it’s hard to see it that way because everyone comes into the game as a recruit – including the ones who eventually become recruiters.

line: I Brought in weed, got rid of that dirt for them
vault_lines: I Brought in weed, got rid of that dirt for them
meaning:
Weeds grow in the dirt, and in the hood playing around with drugs can draw unwanted attention, or “dirt” in the form of a hit or robbery target.

If the hustlers he has given consignment to find themselves in local trouble, he makes it disappear. For a fee, of course.

line: Plus if they was short with cheese I would work with them
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
As a major supplier if his retail drug-dealers did not have the “cheese” (cash) up-front to pay for his cocaine, he would work out a financing arrangement. He may allow them to work on consignment: fronting them the drugs as a loan, which they repay with the profits they make.

At first blush this seems to be a violation of the 6th Crack Commandment, but Jay is dealing to retailers rather than crackheads here.

It also mirrors his generosity in the rap game.

S. Carter, ghost writer, and for the right price
I can even make YO' shit tighter

Maryland is conveniently close to Virginia.

“Used to sell drugs in Virginia” (one interpretation of HOVA besides “Jehovah” is “Hustler of Virginia”). Jay spent a lot of time in Virginia early in his life as a hustler.

It’s become a common introduction for this track at live shows.

line: The flow of the century Always timeless
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
During Decoded Jay devoted an entire paragraph to flow, indicating the depth of thought he’s given the technique.

The flow isn’t like time, it’s like life. It’s like a heartbeat or the way you breathe, it can jump, speed up, slow down, stop, or pound right through like a machine. Flow is what we do with the time, how we live through it.

He regularly claims to have the best flow, and tracks like “Hovi Baby” exist almost entirely to showcase his ability on a beat.

line: Welcome everybody to the 8th Wonder of the world

There are generally regarded to be 7 Wonders of the World.  These are construction projects that were so incredible, that even with modern technology, it seems impossible that they would exist.  Jay Z is now the 8th Wonder.

 + 

8th Wonder was also the name he planned on calling his classic, “retirement” record The Black Album.

line: I got the most incredible Roots band with me tonight y’all
vault_lines: I got the most incredible Roots band with me tonight y'all
meaning:
The Roots are a hip hop group from Philadelphia, now occupying the house band slot on The Late Night Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.

Drummer Questlove in his book Mo Meta Blues claimed to at first be skeptical of Jay’s brand of hip hop, and questioned whether he should participate in the MTV Unplugged show.


When he got the offer to do MTV Unplugged He wanted us to be his backing band. I’m ashamed to admit that I panicked. Even though I liked his record, even though I was developing a tremendous respect for him as an artist, I still felt that he was the antichrist to a certain kind of hip hop fan. Admiring him was one thing – but collaborating with him? That seemed like it could be a real train-wreck of critical signifiers.

We ended up backing him on the Unplugged special, and then a bit later I was his musical director for the Madison Square Garden show.

line: Tonight I’m (H to the izz-O, V to the izz-A) You gotta love that
vault_lines: You gotta love that
meaning:
With a little rap flair, spelling out Hova (H-O-V-A), one of his nicknames

Hova is short for Jehovah, a name for God.

Of course, Biggie used the “X to the izz-Y” concept before Jay, in “Victory”.

line: Iceberg,
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
The track “Who You Wit” first introduced “Iceberg Slim,” a nickname bestowed thanks to Jay’s liking for Iceberg clothing.



During the 90s the popularity of the fashion house exploded with rappers and fans. Jay attempted to make money from the company, but was only offered “free clothing and use of their private plane.” This sowed the seeds for his ultra successful Rocawear clothing line.

line: Sometimes they call me Young Hov
vault_lines: Sometimes they call me Young Hov
meaning: Young Hov seems to have originated around The Dynasty, not long before this album was released. Calling himself “Young” became a habit that he continued right up until Blueprint 3 in 2009. “Hov” refers to Jehovah, another word for God. He received the nickname early in his career due to his ability to spit rhymes without a pen or a pad.

line: Sometimes they call me Jigga
vault_lines: Sometimes they call me Jigga
meaning:
Jigga allegedly comes from his mother, who began using the nickname early in his life.

Another source claims Jay gave himself the nickname, and used it to replace the n word on radio singles, notably “N-What, N- Who (Originator ‘99)”.

line: I go by a couple of names People call me a lot of names, couple to my face you know Sometimes they call me Jay Z
vault_lines: I go by a couple of names
meaning:
The many monikers of Shawn Corey Carter. “Camel” is a name few would dare utter to his face in 2001, but Jigga, Young Hov and Iceberg are all admissible.

Jay Z is the rap name he took on in the late 80s, a mash of his hustling name Jazzy. Many speculated Jay Z is an homage to mentor Jaz-O, though this has never been confirmed.

line: Welcome ladies and gentleman once again As if we never left It’s MTV Unplugged I’ll be your host this evening
vault_lines: I'll be your host this evening
meaning:
This was the second generation of the classic MTV Unplugged series, though not the first foray in to hip hop. Yo! MTV Raps Unplugged featuring LL Cool J, A Tribe Called Quest and De La Soul aired in 1991.

The intro takes the flow and feel from the original track.

line: Welcome to Jay Z’s poetry reading Halt, who goes there? Do this, do this {*does poetry snaps, audience follows*} It was the winter It was cold It was the cold winter
vault_lines: Welcome to Jay Z's poetry reading
meaning:
Jay mimics the classic Def Poetry Jam, a series that was well in to production during the MTV Unplugged recording. Hosted by Yasiin Bey, the show gained popularity from 2002 to 2007 and even prompted a spin off, Def Comedy Jam.

In subsequent years Jay would fight for the poetic value of his music, with his book Decoded delving deep in to the meaning behind his iconic verses.

I hope readers take away from this book that rap is poetry. It’s thought-provoking; there’s thought behind it, there’s great writing in rap as well. You never hear rappers being compared for like the greatest rap writers of all time. 

His ham-fisted turn at poetry in the intro is likely just tongue and cheek.

Ain’t nothing cool about carrying a strap

Specifically Apartment 4B. Right in the heart of Marcy Projects.

Utilising two double meanings to highlight the poverty he faced. Roaches can mean both marijuana cigarettes and cockroaches, and rats refer to both the vermin and those who snitch on dealers, making the location even more fraught.

A crack addict will do anything for a fix. It’s depressing to think of someone selling their mothers possessions for drugs, but it was reality for those in the Projects.

line: We can talk, but money talks, so talk more bucks

The power of Roc-A-Fella records at the time was obvious. He was hailed as “The King of Rap” by news outlets, and his influence was huge.

Dame was quoted at the time:

Entrepreneurial, hustler, say it whatever you want to say it – just that hunger to make money, and to make your situation better.

Jay is willing to sit down and have a conversation with those he feels have wronged him, but as long as there are dollar signs involved, otherwise there’s no point.

line: I do this for my culture, to let ’em know What a nigga look like when a nigga in a roadster
vault_lines: I do this for my culture, to let 'em know
meaning:
Even in 2001 he recognised his life story and his achievements were something to aspire to for young Black males. Not only that, the mention of “culture” adds a hip hop edge, and his business dealings and eventual success map out the “blueprint” for young rappers to follow in their career.

Jay is either referring to a Ferrari Testarossa or a  “roadster”, an open two-seat car sometimes also called a spider or spyder – and would most likely be referring to a Porsche. Jigga has often expressed a penchant for expensive cars during this period.

line: Not guilty, y’all got to feel me
vault_lines: Not guilty, y'all got to feel me
meaning:
“Not guilty” has been a refrain on multiple Jay songs, from “22 Two’s” to “Guilty Until Proven Innocent.” It’s unclear what legal troubles he faced during 1996 when “22 Two’s” was recorded. The case “Guilty Until Proven Innocent” refers to is much easier to trace; the stabbing charges from his tussle with Lance “Un” Rivera would be at the forefront of his mind for many years after its December 1999 occurrence.



Jay would plead guilty to a lesser charge of third-degree assault the month after the release of The Blueprint, receiving three years probation and avoiding possible jail time of 15 years.

line: Brought in weed, got rid of that dirt for them
vault_lines: Brought in weed, got rid of that dirt for them
meaning:
Weeds grow in the dirt, and in the hood playing around with drugs can draw unwanted attention, or “dirt” in the form of a hit or robbery target.

If the hustlers he has given consignment to find themselves in local trouble, he makes it disappear. For a fee, of course.

line: The flow of the century Always timeless Hov
vault_lines: The flow of the century
meaning:
During Decoded Jay devoted an entire paragraph to flow, indicating the depth of thought he’s given the technique.

The flow isn’t like time, it’s like life. It’s like a heartbeat or the way you breathe, it can jump, speed up, slow down, stop, or pound right through like a machine. Flow is what we do with the time, how we live through it.

He regularly claims to have the best flow, and tracks like “Hovi Baby” exist almost entirely to showcase his ability on a beat.

As Hov tells XXL:

I remember having the hook, [and] it was too repetitive. Telling Tone, “Man, this record could be something, but the hook—‘H to the Izzo’—sounds like the verses. It just keeps going. It needs something to break it up.” Tone was like, “Put the girl under it.” The best and the worst mistake we ever made—shit. And I was like, “Yo, you a genius. That’s why you in here.”… I got sued messing with Tone on “Izzo,” because he had a girl with him who we put under the hook. She said she created that hook.

The beat samples multiple elements from the Jackson 5’s “I Want You Back” including vocals and strings.
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s3Q80mk7bxE

Hov talking about the sample:

[M]y mom and pop had an extensive record collection. So Michael Jackson and Stevie Wonder, and all those sounds and souls – and Motown etc., etc. – filled the house. So I was very familiar with the song when Kanye bought me the sample. It was just such an interesting and fresh take on it that I immediately was drawn to it.

The track helped establish the sped-up soul sample as a significant tool of production and Kanye himself said:

Brought back the soul

The drums may be an interpolation/replayed sample of the drums from “Xxplosive” by Dr. Dre, which Kanye has admitted to biting before. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qs2g0NR71pw#t=39
With piano slides and strings on top.

line: Is not real to me, therefore he doesn’t exist So poof, vamoose, son of a bitch
vault_lines: Is not real to me, therefore he doesn't exist
meaning:
Haters aren’t even on the radar, a policy he’d relax in the coming years.

The message plays off “Cogito ergo sum”, a proposition by Descartes that states “I think, therefore I am.” Anyone not feeling Jay doesn’t exist in his mind, and so ceases to exist.

‘'Vamoose’‘ comes from spanish ’‘vamos’‘, which means ’‘let’s go’‘ “Vamoose” is also the name of a bus line that runs direct service between NYC and the Maryland/DC/Virginia area, (which started running 3 years after this song was recorded)



Even the bus company is trying to make Jay have unintended entendres.

line: Welcome, ladies and gentlemen To the eighth wonder of the world
vault_lines: Welcome, ladies and gentlemen
meaning:
The Wonders of the World are constructions built in previous centuries so remarkable that it seems impossible they could exist. Hov is claiming to be the Eighth Wonder of the World, an extremely boastful line he can back up with facts.



Hov first claimed this Eighth Wonder status on “Celebration” in 1998; and at one point he was even planning to name his 2003 retirement album 8th Wonder.

line: Pay us like you owe us for all the years that you hoed us
vault_lines: Pay us like you owe us for all the years that you hoed us
meaning:
As he has done throughout his career, Jay is accusing music executives of treating rappers like hoes. Kendrick Lamar’s message on To Pimp A Butterfly took a similar route.

Hoe’d is also a near homophone of hold. Many record labels hold artists back, deciding not to release records that an artist has slaved hard over in case of poor sales. For example, this was an issue for The LOX and their relationship with Bad Boy Entertainment.

It could also refer to slavery, and the way Black people were held against their will, forced to work for zero pay. His opening line is “I do this for my culture.”

line: Yeah, Hov is back, life stories told through rap Niggas acting like I sold you crack (Yeah) Like I told you sell drugs, no, Hov did that So hopefully you won’t have to go through that
vault_lines: Yeah, Hov is back, life stories told through rap
meaning:
He raps about his experiences selling crack so you can get the experience without going out there and doing it themselves. But just because he is talking about crime, he isn’t endorsing it.
He is addressing accusations of poorly representing his community and perpetuating a glorification of criminal behaviour. There’s a scene in Fade To Black where he addresses this explicitly, saying he provides both sides of the argument: pleasure and pain.

During “Dope Man” Jay directly addresses the claim that he promotes criminal behaviour.

How come, you label your brand of dope
“Volume 1” and spread it through the slums?
Fed it to the young with total disregard
Your honor, the State seeks the maximum charge

line: Show ’em how to move in a room full of vultures Industry shady, it need to be taken over
vault_lines: Show 'em how to move in a room full of vultures
meaning:
Throughout his career, Jay has criticized the establishment of the music industry. In ‘96, he called for black-owned record labels; in 2015 he launched Tidal to compete with Spotify. That’s consistent with metaphorically comparing the music industry to vultures – disgusting scavengers, eating the flesh of struggling artists. Jay is trying to show other artists how to handle the corporate world – by dominating it.

Note the similarity to a Q-Tip line from “Check The Rhime” by A Tribe Called Quest:

Industry rule number four thousand and eighty
Record company people are shady

Although this line is often interpreted as a shot at Eminem, also known as Slim Shady, this is unlikely. Eminem featured on “Renegade”, so it’s unlikely Jay had beef with him. “Shady” is just a part of his lexicon.

line: Can’t leave rap alone, the game needs me
vault_lines: Can't leave rap alone, the game needs me
meaning:
But Hov would soon “retire”!

He would break up with the female representation of the rap game on “Dear Summer.”

But Hov would really prove this line true when he unretired to release Kingdom Come in 2006.

Eminem interpolated this line on his song “Business.”

line: I’ve seen hoop dreams deflate like a true fiend’s weight
vault_lines: I've seen hoop dreams deflate like a true fiend's weight
meaning:
Jay has seen kids in the ghetto with aspirations to be a basketball star ruined, either by violence or prison.

A true fiend (someone addicted to crack) loses a lot of weight. The word “deflate” also evokes a mental image of a basketall losing air.

Weight is also slang for money, “getting ya weight up.” A true drug fiend’s money is going to deflate because all of his money is going towards drugs.

Another interpretation is “weight” as slang for drugs, which a true fiend would go through very quickly.

Also, Hoop Dreams is a 1994 documentary following two basketball prospects in Chicago and their dream of becoming professional basketball players.

line: Cops want to knock me, D.A. wants to box me in But somehow, I beat them charges like Rocky
vault_lines: Cops want to knock me, D.A. wants to box me in
meaning:
Police want to “knock” (arrest) Jay and the District Attorney wants to put him in jail.

Rocky Balboa, the fictional boxing hero of the Rocky movies, dodged his share of punches from his fighting opponents.



Tried to “box me in”, I “beat” them charges like Rocky. He describes his fight with the law as a boxing metaphor. One of Jay’s favourite sports is boxing, he spoke about it extensively in Decoded and expanded into boxing management with his Roc Nation Sports arm.

His trial for the alleged stabbing of Lance “Un” Rivera wasn’t him beating the charges, rather he took probation by pleading guilty, in the knowledge if he had attempted a not guilty plea he may have faced jail time.

line: Wasn’t born hustlers, I was birthing ’em
vault_lines: Wasn't born hustlers, I was birthing 'em
meaning:
A play on the “born hustler” idea in rap: drug-dealing can’t be taught, you have to grow up in the ghetto to do it well. You learn from experience, not books or schools.

Jay-Z was a supplier, he was turning his middlemen into hustlers.

In Decoded Jay explained the nature of passing his skills on to the younger generation:

They know that if they find the right kid, they can put him under their tutelage and he’ll get it fast, step right into the rhythm of the life. If that sounds predatory, it’s because recruiting new workers is one of the most predatory aspects of the game. When you’re doing it, it’s hard to see it that way because everyone comes into the game as a recruit – including the ones who eventually become recruiters.

line: Plus if they was short with cheese, I would work with them
vault_lines: Plus if they was short with cheese, I would work with them
meaning:
As a major supplier, if Jay’s retail drug-dealers did not have the “cheese” (cash) up front to pay for his drugs, he would work out a financing arrangement. Perhaps they worked on consignment: Hov would front them the drugs as a loan, and they’d repay him with the profits they made.

At first blush this line seems to be a violation of the 6th Crack Commandment, but Jay is dealing to retailers here, not to drug addicts.

line: Was herbing ’em in the home of the Terrapins Got it dirt cheap for them
vault_lines: Was herbing 'em in the home of the Terrapins
meaning:
The Maryland Terrapins, commonly referred to as the Terps, represent the University of Maryland in NCAA sports.



Jay-Z wrote in Decoded that he first followed the drug market to New Jersey, where his partner DeHaven Irby had family, and then down to Maryland:

One of the benefits of me and my crew working out of town was that I never had to be under the thumb of one of the big Brooklyn bosses. We were like pioneers on the frontier, staking out new territory where we could run things ourselves.

There Irby would introduce Shawn to one of his closest friends, Emory “Vegas” Jones grew up in Cambridge in Maryland, which is about a hour and a half from the University. Hov would stay with Vegas when he was drug-running along the I-95, stopping to cook crack at his house on Robbins Street.

“Herbin'” suggests he was selling the University students marijuana, as suggested again just two lines down.

line: Used to dribble down in VA
vault_lines: used to dribble down in VA
meaning:
“Used to sell drugs in Virginia” (one interpretation of HOVA besides “Jehovah” is “Hustler of Virginia”). Jay spent a lot of time in Virginia early in his life as a hustler.

Many rappers (cf. Notorious BIG) claim to have sold a lot of drugs in Southern/Midwestern states

“Dribble” can be a pun on “moving rock”, “rock” being slang for a basketball as well as crack cocaine

In his book Decoded, Jay-Z retells of him playing basketball for fun in Virginia while on his excursions for hustling.

line: For shizzle, my nizzle,
vault_lines: For shizzle, my nizzle,
meaning:
“Fo shizzle, my nizzle” stands for “For sure, my nigga”, a phrase popularized by the rapper Snoop Dogg.

Snoop did not invent it, however; the earliest known usage of -izzle speak was in 1981 by Frankie Smith in his hit single “The Double Dutch Bus” (famously sampled by Missy Elliot in “Pass That Dutch”)

“Status quo” means the existing state of affairs. At the time label owners were hurting artists with harsh contracts and withholding payments of royalties.

As the owner of a major rap label, Jay now has industry clout. When other labels come to him for features or distribution deals, he keeps his own prices extra high as payback. “Rappers Delight”, one of the earliest rap songs, originally by Grandmaster Caz, a member of The Cold Crush Brothers, was just one example of artists not receiving their due compensation for work they did.

line: See what you got here’s a full blown twister, you nuttin’ but hot air
vault_lines: See what you got here's a full blown twister, you nuttin' but hot air
meaning:
“Twister” is another term for a Tornado, a weather phenomenon. In order for a Tornado to be created, hot air mixes with cold air. Hot air will rise above cold air, so as the hot air rises, pushing cold air towards the ground, it gains power and velocity.

In this lyrical extract, Jay is the twister, either via his force and power in the game, or his lyrical “tongue twisters”. His enemy is merely “hot air”, a term applied to someone who is speaking for the sake of speaking. With hot air alone, a twister can’t form.

line: This is Jay everyday (Day) No days off, Ferris Bueller nigga

meaning: Ferris Bueller’s Day Off is a wildly popular film from the mid-80s. Jay also used “this is Jay everyday” on his 2001 track “Never Change”.

line: Don’t get carried away, you a mule nigga (Mule nigga)
vault_lines: Don't get carried away, you a mule nigga (Mule nigga)
meaning: “Mule” takes on two meanings. He references the animal, which is commonly used to transport goods or belongings, and the term given to people who physically transport drugs across long distances, known as drug mules. The implication is Jay and Beans are at the highest level of their craft, and anyone challenging them is getting “carried away”, believing they’re bigger or better than they truly are. It echoes a similar sentiment to Jay’s song “Only A Customer”.

line: It’s a secret society, all we ask is trust

A “secret society” is an organization whose members are sworn to secrecy about its activities. To be welcomed into the fray at Roc-A-Fella Records and witness the lifestyle they lead, one must act in a trust-worthy and loyal manner.

The second meaning refers to the overall message of the song. The song is (for the most part) about being a killer. So when Ja looks in the mirror he sees a good looking man and a literal killer.

line: Ya co-D,

meaning: A co-D is short for codefendant. A codefendant is “one of two or more individuals or entities accused of the same crime or sued in the same lawsuit. They are jointly involved in the legal proceedings, sharing the same formal accusation in a criminal case or the same legal claim in a civil case.” A codefendant could be scene as a bad thing for many reasons, one being if they want to place all the blame on you, which could be why Ja Rule might not like a co-D.

line: Y’all don’t understand we want y’all all to hate it (It’s murda) Murder Incorporated (It’s murda) In crime we all related (It’s murda) You niggas see if y’all can fade it

meaning:
In 1999 none of these artists were suffering from a lot of hate. Jay had gone 5 times platinum, X had released 2 number one albums in a year, and Ja Rule had a huge buzz after being signed to Def Jam, featuring on Jay’s Hard Knock Life tour and his feature on “Can I Get A…”.

The hate would come later, as Murder Inc, completely separate from Jay and X, fell into sharp decline.

line: Shit, I got the feds wearin’ riot suits

meaning:
It’s kill or be killed in this environment, and Jay places his own life, and that of Ja and DMX, above their collective enemies.

Jay was the only rapper of the three who was the boss of a label. While this isn’t intended to throw shade at his collaborators, positioning himself as the shot-caller might have bred some animosity.

This is why he’s able to approve hits, both in the street and on wax. In charge of artists like Memphis Bleek, it’s part of his job as executive producer to sign off on singles and track listings, and the success of those early albums helped to “dead” the competition.

line: I dip, squat, then post up with the toast up

Jay is ducking the shells from his competition. When they have run out of ammunition, he jumps up with his weapon and returns fire.

“Post up” also means to both to claim a spot, or a corner, for drug dealing, and in basketball to stand near the foul line as a defensive player to block an attacker.

line: Since you couldn’t fuck with a third of us

Although they never managed to record an album together or get off the ground as a group, they did refer to themselves as a collective at one point, going by the name “Murder Inc” in reference to the label that Irv Gotti had set up. He was the driving force behind the trio.

This lyric would prove true, as all three achieved an incredible amount of individual success.

line: I don’t know what’s wrong with me, but it seems like since you heard of us Y’all niggas turned into murderers

Unfortunately these lines continue to ring true throughout X’s career, with multiple arrests and drug addictions forcing his fans to ask the same question.

Did he inspire criminal activity? Tracks like 1998’s “Bring Your Whole Crew” are violent on a level that his two collaborators never managed:

You be a dead motherfucker, red motherfucker

meaning:
X had a difficult childhood, running afoul of the law often, and relying on the streets to raise him.

He was born in December, so it’s likely he means that from birth he was protecting himself with a weapon. He also plays on being born in the coldest month, December, meaning he needed to keep heat on him to survive.

line: They got my back against the building, I’m the villain that’s creeping around corners Like, shorty, if you see them niggas creeping around, warn us
vault_lines: They got my back against the building, I'm the villain that's creeping around corners
meaning:

meaning: On this verse Jay-Z explicitly describes an affair between him and a woman who has a partner. This led to Nas directly engaging in the beef with Hov, which had been quietly developing between the two New York rappers over the previous four years.

It’s still the lowest-charting album of Jay’s career. And of its four singles, only one (“Ain’t No Nigga”) peaked in the top 50 of Billboard’s Hot 100, and only “Dead Presidents” went Gold.

This is a reference to Tom, Dick & Harry’s, a well-known sneaker store in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn.

Jay Z shot a scene to his 1998 film “Streets Is Watching” inside of Tom D’s.

Chain stores like Footlocker and Champs Sports are forced to sell sneakers on a release date determined by the manufacture, but mom and pop stores like Tom D’s often sell Air Jordans and other coveted sneakers way before their scheduled release date.

They often charge customers a little more than the suggested retail price— but for sneaker heads who want exclusive kicks and make his friends mad with jealously, it’s totally worth it.

“Hand It Down” was released in September 1998, so it’s possible that Bleek is referencing the Air Jordan XIV model, which was released that same year.

line: On my mental piano Got a strange way of seeing life, like I’m Stevie Wonder with beads under the do-rag Intuition is there, even when my vision’s impaired, yeah
vault_lines: on my mental piano
meaning:
Stevie Wonder is an American musician who released an album in 1976 titled Songs in the Key of Life. Wonder’s vision is impaired because of his blindness, and he has to rely on his intuition and other senses to navigate the world. Hov relates to Wonder in how it was for him on the streets during his previous drug-dealing career: he had to rely on his instincts to survive the imminent dangers and anticipate any adversity from others. Hov had the ability to understand the drug and rap games instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.



Within the reference Jay also manages to drop a pun on the implied homophone of beads, which Wonder wore on his braids, and “beeds” which used to be a common term for “nappy hair,” like Jay would have under his du-rag.

line: The theme song to The Sopranos Plays in the key of life

meaning:
The Sopranos, the legendary TV series about mob boss Tony Soprano balancing family life with the violent realities of organized crime, opens each episode with the theme song “Woke Up This Morning (Chosen One)” by Alabama 3, which famously begins:

Woke up this morning, got yourself a gun

The imagery ties both to Tony Soprano’s world and to Jay’s own early reality growing up in Marcy Projects: waking up each day in an environment where carrying a gun was part of survival. Notably, Nas later sampled the track on 2001’s “Got Ur Self a Gun.”

Tony alongside Christopher Moltisanti & Silvio Dante in The Sopranos.

The phrase “key of life” nods to Stevie Wonder’s classic 1976 album Songs in the Key of Life, which Jay reinforces in the following line when he directly references Stevie. The double reference positions Jay’s worldview as a blend of mob boss (The Sopranos) and musical genius (Stevie).

Hov greeting Stevie, joined by Jamie Foxx and Beyoncé.

2. Gear as in fresh clothes. Jay’s competitors are in a nice suit to collect the award but their music is wack, so it’s a waste.

As a famous and prominent figure in hip-hop Jay’s music has often been made the scapegoat in controversies about some of rap’s less proud lyrical moments, even being targeted by Oprah. Jay’s offended that people are missing the point – the controversy wasn’t about the word “hoes”, it was about the use of a racial epithet by a white man, and he is sick of hip-hop generally, and his lyrics specifically, being dragged into the debate.

Believe nothing, no matter where you read it or who has said it, not even if I have said it, unless it agrees with your own reason and your own common sense. – Buddha

meaning: Dope is a slang term meaning cool, so him saying that he is so dope is also him saying “Damn i’m really cool dawg!?!”

vault_lines: And your soul is in control, trying to lead it from me
meaning:
Jay’s hold over this woman was through her emotions. Once her heart’s allegiance changed, she was lost to him.

“D” refers to both the drug (heroin/his music) and “The Dick”. He’s no longer able to keep her by his side with his sexual prowess.

It’s a little seperation but I know how to fix the situation
Mami just sufferin from love deprevation
So I gotta give her thug reperations
Put it in the life until love leg is shakin
Slow and passionate, ‘til we forget what happens

line: How could you leave me? I thought that you needed me! When the world got too much and you pleaded with me
vault_lines: How could you leave me?
meaning:
Jay again inhabits his 3 persona’s here. First, he reacts to the poor reception that Kingdom Come received upon release, questioning why his good press deserted him.

He then speaks of the spurned lover who was left by the woman of his dreams.

Finally, he returns to heroin. Clearly the woman has listened to the conscience that interfered in the second verse and has begun to attempt recovery.

line: I know what you like, I am your prescription I’m your physician, I’m your addiction
vault_lines: And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know (Uhh, I know what you like)
meaning:
One of the more confident lines in Jay’s back catalogue.

Prescribing a drug that someone is withdrawing from will immediately remove their symptoms. Jay can speak with authority on addiction, although his haven’t been on the substance variety.

Take one more toke and I leave that weed alone, man
It got me going, shit

His hugely successful recording career is a testament to his knowledge of what listeners want to hear from a rap album.

That’s the shit I’m sprinklin'
The album width to keep the registers ringin'

line: Now that feelin’ got you tripping, you don’t wanna feel no different This here lust has got you itching, nose wide open and it’s dripping
vault_lines: Now that feelin' got you tripping, you don't wanna feel no different
meaning:
The subject has just injected for the first time, the most effective way of removing their pain. Many junkies describe their first rush as the best, a feeling they spend their life chasing and never fully achieving again. “Chasing the Dragon” is a term commonly associated with it.

One former addict said this about their first time:

I wanted to do nothing else but feel that way. I decided almost immediately that this was going to be my life.

Itching and a runny nose are just two of the myriad of withdrawal symptoms associated with Heroin use.

line: That Black Rain will take away your pain Just for one night, baby, take me in vein
vault_lines: That Black Rain will take away your pain
meaning:
“Black Rain” is another word for black tar heroin, simply another form of the drug.

Heroin can be smoked, swallowed, snorted, or injected. Injecting holds the greatest “rush”, but is also the most dangerous in terms of addiction (to that rush) and physical health (diseases can be transmitted through dirty needles). Heroin users who are injecting maybe be considered as worse off than those who take it in other ways.

line: This is about lust, cold sweats occur when I’m not with her My presence is a must- must- must-
vault_lines: My presence is a must- must- must-
meaning: Heroin withdrawals are not pleasant at all. Cold sweats are the beginning of the problem. A cold sweat can also be induced by anxiety or fear, and the persona Jay is speaking intimately to is also lusting after him physically, so if he’s not around it causes panic.

line: She leans for me Morning, she rush for my touch
vault_lines: She leans for me
meaning:
The “dope fiend lean” is a move reserved to the most impaired users. Jay described “leaners” in his book Decoded,

It was the seventies and heroin was still heavy in the hood, so we would dare one another to push a leaning nodder off a bench the way kids on farms tip sleeping cows.

The “heroin rush” is the feeling of the opioid hitting the bloodstream and working it’s way through the body. Morning’s tend to be a desperate time for junkies, as they come off a heroin fast and search for their next hit.

line: Uhh, she wants that old thing back Uh, uh, uh, she want those heroin tracks She likes me, she fiends for me nightly
vault_lines: Uhh, she wants that old thing back
meaning:
Borrowing a sentiment from Notorious B.I.G.’s “One More Chance”, Jay details the well known addict phenomenon that the first high (especially on Heroin) is the best. It’s an incredibly difficult scenario to replicate, and results in consistently higher concentrations of the drug to find the feeling again.

He directly references heroin by highlighting the tracks that line a junkie’s arm from their needle use. He plays on the word “tracks” to also mean music: Jay’s music is so good it’s like heroin to the listener.

line: And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know (Uhh, I know what you like) And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know (I know what you love) Everything you like, everything you love (Baby you like ....Hov’!) Everything you like, everything you love (Baby you love ....Hov’! Baby you love, hehehe, uhh) And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know (Baby you love ....Hov’!) Everything you like, everything you love (Baby you like ....Hov’! Baby you like ....Hov’!) Everything you like, everything you love, damn (Baby you like ....Hov’!)
vault_lines: And I know, and I know, and I know, and I know (Uhh, I know what you like)
meaning:
Jay inhabits 3 separate identities here: He is the drug Heroin, he is the hustler selling it to his fiends, and he is the lover that this woman desires.

As all three, he has intimate knowledge of the wants (and needs) of the fiend attracted to him.

line: Although it never be, the feeling is fleeting Shopping’s like copping, you constantly need it I’m never around, you constantly seek it
vault_lines: Although it never be, the feeling is fleeting
meaning:
The feeling from the first verse has left. Heroin only lasts a few hours in your system, and although the warmth from a fresh pair of shoes is an individual experience, buyers remorse can set in suddenly and unexpectedly.  Shopping becomes like buying the drugs, taking them home, opening them up and ingesting them.

Jay as a lover can be scarce as well.

Girlfriend didn’t believe me when I said I’d be back in a little
Cause I had the crisp tee on with the crease in the middle
Plus a fresh cut and the freezin icicles
On my wrist, on my hand, that’s when shit hit the fan
Said, “You never spend timey, what’s up with that?”

line: But when that medicine’s felt We’re back together, don’t ever leave me Don’t ever let ’em tell you that you’ll never need me
vault_lines: But when that medicine's felt
meaning: Jay-Z is personifying the drug heroin itself, (in conjunction with the last two lines) speaking to the user. The user in her sober mind wants to quit, but when she relapses, her addiction is just reinforced. The drug whispers in her ear to distrust authority figures and give in to the pleasure.

line: It’s so much fun, you shun therapy
vault_lines: It's so much fun, you shun therapy
meaning:
A double entendre. Jay utilises the near homophone shun/shawn (carter) to describe himself as the therapy.

And his subject is enjoying their addiction so much, any attempts at intervention are supremely unsuccessful.

line: Now your body is shaking, trying to free it of me
vault_lines: Now your body is shaking, trying to free it of me
meaning:
Withdrawal symptoms include:

•Restlessness
•Insomnia
•Diarrhea
•Vomiting
•Cold flashes with goose bumps
•Kicking movements
•Muscle and bone pain

Major withdrawal symptoms peak between 48 and 72 hours after the last dose and subside after about a week.

line: Who helped you immediately? How speedy of me! How could you deny me so vehemently?
vault_lines: How could you leave me?
meaning:
Heroin is known for it’s fast acting properties; sometimes effects can be felt just seconds after injection. The drug-addicted woman in question is now “speedballing,” that is, snorting and injecting cocaine and heroin at the same time.

I can rap … I’ve said a lot of words in my career. I got my words. I used vehemently in a rhyme, you know. I got a lot of words. I got a vast vocabulary.

line: My China White, ’til we D.O.A Its Montega forever, baby, lets get away...
vault_lines: My China White, 'til we D.O.A
meaning:
China White is a stronger form of heroin than the previously mentioned “Black Rain” black tar variety. As a result, it is much more likely the addict will end up “D.O.A.,” Dead on Arrival, if they are injecting China White.

Montega is another word for heroin, as well as sounding like “Montego”, a beautiful holiday destination in Jamaica. Jay equates his love, his music, and the drug to a lifelong vacation on an untouched beach…



Who wouldn’t want that for the rest of their lives?

line: You’ll never be down, I know where your peak is 9 1/2 weeks is better than 12-steps I keep trying to remind you to keep telling yourself Now your conscience is interfering, like “Better yourself!” Like you better get help
vault_lines: I know what you like, I am your prescription
meaning:
9½ Weeks is a film where a man dominates a woman sexually to such a stage that she becomes physically dependent on him. Jay plays off this dynamic, describing the way a drug will entice a victim and ensnare them in a constant battle to get high.

The 12 Steps program is popularized by Alcoholics Anonymous, but can be modified to help treat any addiction. The subjects conscience recognizes the need for change, and the drug senses this and pulls back.

line: Like Louboutins with the red bottoms You gotta have ’em, you glad you got ’em Like every color Giuseppe’s, your guilty pleasure is me
vault_lines: Like Louboutins with the red bottoms
meaning:
A brand of shoe synonymous with high class women as well as weekend shopaholics.

Giuseppe’s are shoes by Italian designer Giuseppe Zanotti, a friend and associate of Kanye West.

Shopping addiction is a genuine disorder that falls on the addictive spectrum. Jay has shown a propensity to lace his women with expensive gifts:

Might buy you Crist', but that about it
Might light your wrist, but that about it
Fuck it, I might wife you and buy you nice whips

As a result, women flock to him.

line: In any form, I’m giving you sweet dreams That Sugar Hill, she call me her sweet thing
vault_lines: In any form, I'm giving you sweet dreams
meaning:
Whether it be music, drugs, or romance, Jay is putting his subject at ease and taking away their pain.

The “sweet dreams” refers to the American Dream he is promoting. He’s help made success attainable for young black men in the hood.

“Sugar Hill” takes on 4 meanings. It is another word for Heroin, as well as being a 1993 movie starring Wesley Snipes as a drug dealer who attempts to exit the game.

It’s also a predominantly black Manhattan neighbourhood, as well as being a reference to the Sugarhill Gang.

line: Bonita Applebum, I gotta put you on If I didn’t when we cutting, the feeling’ll be too strong
vault_lines: Bonita Applebum, I gotta put you on
meaning:
“Bonita Applebum” is a song by A Tribe Called Quest.

Bonita Applebum, you gotta put me on
Bonita Applebum I said you gotta put me on
Bonita Applebum, you gotta put me on
Bonita, Bonita, Bonita

“Benita” is a common cut added to heroin, purchased from local bodega’s and derived from the Spanish word “Bonita”. It usually refers to Quinine.

Heroin is cut to reduce it’s potency and to increase it’s value. Uncut, pure heroin, the sort that Lucas purchased from Vietnam during American Gangster, can be incredibly dangerous to the uninitiated. Jay dilutes his music in a similar fashion.

I make “Big Pimpin'” or “Give it to Me” one of those
Y'all hail me as the greatest writer of the 21st century
I make some thought provokin shit y'all question whether he fallin off

Give it to me!

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)

vault_lines: Both in the club, high, singing off key
meaning:
Here Jay interpolates the first line of the chorus of Carl Thomas' #1 R&B single “I Wish.” Hov had previously worked with the Bad Boy Records artist on Mic Geronimo’s 1997 track “Single Life.”

“I Wish” was the lead single from Thomas' Platinum-certified debut album Emotional. At the album’s release party Hov sang the album’s praises, saying “it’s the only thing in my deck right now.”




Jay-Z, photographed at the Emotional release party in New York on April 19, 2000.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: Can’t deny me Why would you want to? You need me Why don’t you try me? Baby, you want to believe me (Hov’!)
vault_lines: Why would you want to? You need me
meaning:
Jay’s oscillating sentiments in this track have probably confused this girl to the point of no return. First he’s auditioning as her boyfriend, then he’s a pimp, he then entertains various models before confessing he might wife you.

Despite all this, the hook turns out to be prophetic. A vote for Jay Z was a vote for endless future wealth. Just ask Memphis Bleek.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: Okay, hot Hov’, too hot to hold Ladies love me long time like 2Pac’s soul Only way to roll, Jigga and two ladies
vault_lines: Okay, hot Hov', too hot to hold
meaning:
Despite all this talk of marriage, he brings it back. Like a piece of toast that’s too hot, Jay isn’t held down by women, his options are too numerous. He plays on “roll” and “too hot to hold”, linking to dice. When a gambler is on a winning streak, it’s said the “dice are hot” and they’re “on a heater”. With number 1 albums every year since 1996, Jay’s streak was legendary.

2Pac was selling records long after his death, with R U Still Down? (Remember Me), Until The End of Time, Better Dayz, and Loyal To The Game all going multi-platinum after his death.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: Profess you love to Hov’ and I’ll never let you down Get you bling like the Neptune sound
vault_lines: Profess you love to Hov' and I'll never let you down
meaning:
More third person references. “Never let you down” most likely means he won’t fall off, become poor and unable to lace his woman with incredibly expensive goods.

A quick look at The Neptunes production discography shows a bankable quality: They made charting singles. In this instance Jay compares his woman’s jewellery to the money a Neptunes beat can net an up and coming rapper.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: Might buy you Cris’, but that about it Might light your wrist, but that about it Fuck it, I might wife you and buy you nice whips
vault_lines: Might buy you Cris', but that about it
meaning:
The Cristal is already in play from the first verse, and his mission with that is to impress and intoxicate.

To “light” someone’s wrist is to buy them jewel-encrusted accessories. The illuminating qualities of diamonds were de-constructed in “Girl’s Best Friend”:

When you blush you turn blue if your grade is right
You can light up the whole room, turning day from night

In a mere four lines Jay’s switched from “Big Pimpin'” to marriage. Either he’s been indulging in the intoxicants or he’s met a real woman.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: Yeah, save the narrative, you saving it for marriage Let’s keep it real, ma, you saving it for carats You wanna see how far I’ma go How much I’ma spend but you already know Zip, zero, stingy with dinero
vault_lines: Yeah, save the narrative, you saving it for marriage
meaning:
Playing on ‘carats’ and its homophone ‘carrots,’ the girl in question claims she’s saving herself for nuptials when really she’s just waiting for a man rich enough to come along. It’s a constant theme of Jay’s singles, with “Can I Get A…” addressing the issue and the emotional turmoil it induces in rappers.

During “Big Pimpin'”, Jay raps the following line, which ties in with the ‘carrot’ homophone:

Take ‘em out the hood, keep 'em looking good
But I don’t fucking feed 'em

The girl wants to eat with Jay, but he’s stingy; he doesn’t spend money on women.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)

vault_lines: What do you say, me, you, and your Chloe glasses (Uh-huh)
meaning:
To highlight the credibility of his model claims he shouts out fashion brands Chloe, Prada, Gucci, and Filth Mart, a niche brand of vintage clothing sold exclusively from a single shop-front.

Although Jay would later upgrade his brand names further, the sentiment remains the same. The clothes are meant for the floor anyway.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)

vault_lines: It gets better, ordered another round
meaning:
“Go down” means both the action is about to commence, and fellatio is imminent.

As is his custom, Jay throws a bunch of expensive brand names into the mix. Belvedere Vodka was a particular favourite of his at the time, before his investment in Aramadale. “Crist” refers to Cristal, and with 6 bottles of bubbly and 4 bottles of Vodka to share between Jay and his six model friends, he’s well sorted for alcohol. And although he rarely smokes, marijuana is on deck for those who indulge.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)

Homage to Notorious B.I.G.’s opening to the second verse of his track “The World Is Filled”.

Remy is not his favourite pre-2006 beverage, but it does get mentioned occasionally. After the splash “Big Pimpin'” made, particularly lyrics like:

You know I, thug em, fuck em, love em, leave em
Cause I don’t fucking need em
Take em out the hood, keep em looking good
But I don’t fucking feed em

His treatment of women is clearly not quite at the level he’d eventually reach. While competition (and foes) chase women, Jay has so many he’s fending them off.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: I’m a hustler, baby (Hov’, I’m a hustler) I just want you to know (Hov’, I gotta let you know) It ain’t where I been (It ain’t where I been, Hov’) But where I’m ’bout to go (Top of the world! Young Hova, holla)
vault_lines: I'm a hustler, baby (Hov', I'm a hustler)
meaning:
Jay’s drug dealing past is storied, but by the year 2000 he’d exited the game. His past is irrelevant, and the focus is on the future.

Was this prophetic? At the turn of the millennium, Jay was a certified rap superstar, but his career was about to take flight. He’s currently worth close to a billion dollars when combined with his wife Beyoncé’s net worth, and his business and musical achievements are too numerous to list.

Interestingly, in 2016 he came under fire for his drug dealing past, with personality Tomi Lahren mentioning his drug dealing past in relation to his relationship with his wife. Safe to say his reaction shows he isn’t too perturbed.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: [Produced by The Neptunes]
vault_lines: But be who I am (You know you love me, Hov')
meaning:
Produced by Pharrell and Chad (known collectively as The Neptunes), this beat is one of many responsible for the success of the production duo during the late ‘90s.

Jay Z himself recalls trying to find this beat to go with a hook that Omillio Sparks had written for him:

“I knew right there, those type of songs I know — I made a couple of ‘em — so I know what type of song this is right here. It’s no stopping; I’m unstoppable right now with this song.”

Jay Z goes into further detail about this track and his relationship with Pharrell here.

The track typifies the early Neptunes sound, with artificial clavichord hits and spacious boom bap drums combined with layers of synthetic hand percussion sounds to give the beat a futuristic feel.

During “Ain’t No” this sentiment was more thoroughly dissected:

line: The Peanuts in L.A., bubblin’ in Dublin
vault_lines: The Peanuts in L.A., bubblin' in Dublin
meaning:
Peanuts Nightclub was a fashionable spot in L.A. during the late 90s and early 2000s. “Dublin” is a more hotly contested location, with some claiming it was an exclusive nightclub in L.A. during the mid to late 90s, backed up by this headline.

He may also simply be speaking of the capital city of Ireland, Dublin. Bubblin' means to drink, or to get drunk.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: From Club Cheetah to Club Amnesia
vault_lines: From Club Cheetah to Club Amnesia
meaning:
There’s some conjecture over which nightclubs Jay is actually mentioned here. Club Cheetah is an Atlanta strip club, but it’s also a location in New York mentioned by N.O.R.E. on “Cocaine Business.”

Amnesia Night club still exists in New York, although it’s possible Jay is simply saying he has “club amnesia” from the constant nights spent out partying. He can barely remember the names of the establishments he picks women up in.



Given he’s mentioned being around the world he may be referring to Club Amnesia in Ibiza.

song: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)
line: I’m too cold, Motorola, two-way page me (C’mon)
vault_lines: I'm too cold, Motorola, two-way page me (C'mon)
meaning:
Two-way Pagers were popular during the release of this song, and a Motorola model was featured in the video.

In Steve Stoute’s book The Tanning of America: How Hip-Hop Created a Culture That Rewrote the Rules of the New Economy, Stoute recollects asking Hov to shout out Motorola to improve their brand image. Motorola instantly started selling like hot cakes.

This was the beginning of Jay’s association with mobile brands, in 2013 he began a lucrative deal with Samsung that saw his album certified platinum before it was even released.

line: [Intro: JAY-Z, Future & DJ Khaled]
vault_lines: Uh, uh-uh-uh, DJ Khaled
meaning:
With this record, “I Got the Keys,” I went to go see Hov. You know, any chance I get to see Hov and catch up… He’s my friend, somebody I would reach out to. Not just about making music, but just to check in and catch up and to vibe and to have cloth talk. And at that time we was having some serious cloth talk about a lot of great things that we want to do together. Not even talking about music. I’m talking about just in general and in life.

I was like, “Man I want to play you something.” I said, “I know you ain’t got no speakers.” Because every time I see Jay Z, he ain’t got no speakers in his office. I don’t wanna tell you where I met him at, because it was a secret location, but I knew there wasn’t speakers around. And I’m all about presentation. So I was willing to wait until the right time to play this record, because I’m all about presentation. That’s how I like to do my things.

And he’s like “Nah. I got speakers.” And he had some big speakers, too. I was excited. So I was like, “Yo, I gotta play this!” So I play the record. The intro comes on. And then “Wraith talk, Wraith talk” and that beat comes on. I see him bobbing his head. And then the “I got the keys, the keys, the keys!” I’m trying to play it off and be smooth about it. But I’m like peeping with my eyes to see what he’s doing. Then I see him hearing what Future is saying on the hook, “I got the keys, the keys, the keys!” And I’m watching him. And then I’m seeing the head start moving a little more. So, the instrumental part comes on and I hear him like mumbling.

So, I’m letting it ride. I’m playing it off. I’m just vibing. Knowing it’s great. You know, you gotta be confident. If you ain’t confident, then you’re playing yourself. So, I’m looking to the side still and he’s still mumbling. And I’m watching him do some things! So, boom. The record ends and he’s like, “Man… Leave that for me.” So I was like, trying to be cool about it. You know, certain cloth.

line: That’s too much flavor (What else?) I don’t rap to suckas (Ha!)
vault_lines: That's too much flavor (What else?)

Kool Herc is the the Godfather of Hip-Hop, forming the genre back in the 1970s in The Bronx. He would isolate the instrumental portion of the record, which emphasized the drum beat—the “break”—and switch from one break to another. Using the same two turntable set-up of disco DJs, he would use two copies of the same record to elongate the break. Kool Herc’s announcements and exhortations to dancers (whom he called “break-boys” and “break-girls”) helped lead to the syncopated, rhymed spoken accompaniment we call “rapping.”

Jay never had a true record deal in the beginning of his career. He had a distribution deal, through Priority records, one that, in Jay’s words, was woefully undernourished.

He took a similar route when he approached Iceberg Clothing for an endorsement deal, Iceberg offered them free clothing. Jay and Dame were expecting a proper deal and use of their private jet. This was not forthcoming.

In 1998, Def Jam was sold to Universal Music Group in a $300m deal. At the time, Jay was signed to Def Jam and was dropping new albums yearly, all of which were doing large sales numbers.

Jay-Z has always had much love for his Grandma, Hattie “Yaya” White. Now over 90 years old, she has watched her Grandson rise from living in public housing in the Marcy Projects to being able to afford a penthouse apartment in New York. She knows him as a hardworking and diligent man. Why would anyone not want to live next door to Shawn?

Jay-Z purchased his seventh-floor penthouse on Hudson Street in TriBeCa, Lower Manhattan for $6.85 million in late 2004. Two years earlier in 2002 Hov was in talks with previous owner, advertising executive Peter Arnell, to purchase the apartment – but the original negotiations were sabotaged and derailed by other tenants and the deal fell through.

Some tenants feared Hov would bring his “celebrity lifestyle” to the “placid” halls of their exclusive downtown address. They went so far as to post messages in the lobby warning residents of his “criminal record and lifestyle of knives, guns and violence” and stating “We are of the opinion that due to [Jay-Z’s] lifestyle of violence, if he moves into our building, he will place us in danger.” The Arnell family highly disputed this, and filed a lawsuit in May 2002 against the tenants that interfered in the initial sale.
